title: how the #149 windowsHide A/B repro verifies Windows console-flash on CI
summary: A temporary windows-latest CI workflow (workflow_dispatch-only) can empirically confirm whether a specific child_process option shape flashes a visible console window by polling the real Win32 IsWindowVisible API, but this ONLY worked for the daemon/CLI shape (Node's own detached:true spawn, matching keeper.js's self-relaunch) — three different attempts to reproduce the equivalent condition for hooks/*.mjs (a plain child of Claude Code/Cursor/Codex, Electron GUI-subsystem apps) all came back inconclusive (no window either way), and the likely reason is itself the key finding: windowsHide/CREATE_NO_WINDOW most likely gives a process a HIDDEN console rather than no console at all, so once any ancestor in a chain has one (hidden or visible) its own children just reuse it instead of requesting a new one — meaning this CI technique is structurally unable to isolate the hooks case without literally running Electron. The fix was still applied to hooks/*.mjs (safe no-op if unneeded) and shipped in PR #151; real confirmation deferred to testing on physical Windows hardware.

steps.role: windows-latest job entry point; workflow_dispatch-only (a branch-scoped push trigger was used temporarily to iterate pre-merge, since workflow_dispatch needs the file on the default branch first)
spawns harness.mjs via Node's detached:true+stdio:'ignore' spawn, mirroring keeper.js's own self-relaunch shape — the ONLY mechanism that produced a confirmed flash in this session
runs execFileSync with the option shape under test, with or without windowsHide
attempt #3 at the hooks condition: routes NoConsoleLauncher.exe through the same proven detached:true spawn instead of PowerShell's Start-Process — still inconclusive
compiled /target:winexe (GUI-subsystem) launcher, an independently-built proxy for how Electron apps spawn subprocesses on Windows — used in attempts #2 and #3, neither produced a flash
compiles NoConsoleLauncher.cs via csc.exe, then polls Win32 IsWindowVisible before/after each of the 4 cases (2 daemon-shape + 2 GUI-subsystem-shape)

invariants: workflow_dispatch only lets you trigger workflows already present on the default branch (GitHub platform restriction, confirmed via a live 404) — iterate with a branch-scoped push trigger pre-merge, then drop it once merged

the cleanup step between A/B cases must never Stop-Process match conhost/WindowsTerminal/OpenConsole broadly — those can back the runner's own pwsh session; killing them crashed the very next `node` invocation with a console-pipe error. Only kill the actual test straggler (e.g. ping.exe) by name

a console-flash A/B test only proves something when the code under test is the FIRST thing to request a console in the whole ancestor chain — Node's detached:true spawn (used unpatched, held constant across the A/B pair) satisfies this for the daemon shape, but layering ANY additional console-suppression (CreateNoWindow=true on an intermediate hop, or just launching through an already-console-having process like pwsh) gives that intermediate process a console — hidden or inherited — which then absorbs any downstream child's console need regardless of that child's own windowsHide setting, making the A/B pair indistinguishable

title: how the #149 windowsHide A/B repro verifies Windows console-flash on CI and real hardware
summary: A windows-latest CI workflow (workflow_dispatch-only, now with an explicit `permissions: contents: read` block) empirically confirms whether a child_process option shape flashes a visible console window by polling the real Win32 IsWindowVisible API, and this now works for BOTH shapes coldstart needed to prove: the daemon/CLI shape (Node's own detached:true spawn, matching keeper.js's self-relaunch) AND the hooks/*.mjs shape (a plain child of a console-less Electron host like Claude Code/Cursor). The hooks shape required two failed attempts before landing: a GUI-subsystem (winexe) launcher using .NET's ProcessStartInfo.CreateNoWindow gave the intermediate node.exe a HIDDEN-but-still-attached console rather than none, so its own child (ping.exe) just reused that hidden console regardless of windowsHide — an inconclusive A/B (no flash in either branch). The fix was DetachedLauncher.cs, which calls Win32 CreateProcess directly with the real DETACHED_PROCESS flag (0x8), giving the child genuinely no console object. Under that condition the split is exactly as expected: unpatched flashes, patched doesn't. Confirmed both by the automated IsWindowVisible poll and direct human visual observation on real Windows 11 hardware — this closes the 'hooks shape not independently proven' gap and the fix shipped as part of PR #151 (merged).

steps.role: windows-latest job entry point; workflow_dispatch-only, now scoped to `permissions: contents: read` (added to address a CodeQL missing-workflow-permissions finding on PR #151)
spawns harness.mjs via Node's detached:true+stdio:'ignore' spawn, mirroring keeper.js's own self-relaunch shape — proven mechanism for the daemon-shape A/B
runs execFileSync with the option shape under test, with or without windowsHide

replaces the earlier CreateNoWindow-based launcher; calls Win32 CreateProcess directly with DETACHED_PROCESS so the launched node.exe has genuinely no console object — the actual condition hooks/*.mjs runs under when spawned by a console-less GUI host. This is what finally produced a clean, confirmed flash/no-flash split for the hooks shape
compiles DetachedLauncher.cs via csc.exe, then polls Win32 IsWindowVisible before/after each of the 4 cases (2 daemon-shape via orchestrator.mjs + 2 hooks-shape via DetachedLauncher.exe directly)

invariants: workflow_dispatch only lets you trigger workflows already present on the default branch (GitHub platform restriction) — iterate with a branch-scoped push trigger pre-merge, then drop it once merged

the cleanup step between A/B cases must never Stop-Process match conhost/WindowsTerminal/OpenConsole broadly — those can back the runner's own pwsh session; killing them crashed the very next `node` invocation with a console-pipe error. Only kill the actual test straggler (e.g. ping.exe) by name

a console-flash A/B test only proves something when the code under test is the FIRST thing to request a console in the whole ancestor chain — CreateNoWindow (.NET ProcessStartInfo) suppresses the WINDOW but still leaves a hidden console object attached, which downstream children silently reuse; only the raw Win32 DETACHED_PROCESS flag via CreateProcess gives a child genuinely zero console, which is the condition that makes the A/B pair distinguishable

run watch.ps1 with pwsh (PowerShell 7+), not Windows PowerShell 5.1 — the file is UTF-8 without a BOM (em-dashes in comments), and powershell.exe reads no-BOM files using the system codepage, mangling those bytes and breaking parsing
